title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary: MBA Degree Salary Insights
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary using the 38-hour week. Includes MBA degree salary examples under the Professional Employees Award, casual loading, and super.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work part-time, use your agreed weekly hours instead of 38.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for entitlements casual employees don't receive, such as paid leave. When using our timesheet, you enter your base rate (without casual loading) and check the casual loading box. The tool then adds 25% to that rate. For example, a base rate of $30.00/hour becomes $37.50/hour with casual loading.

faqs.q: How does superannuation factor into my total remuneration?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your gross wages. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay; it's additional.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

If you're negotiating a job offer or comparing roles, understanding how your hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman and most modern awards. The basic conversion is straightforward:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours every week, that's:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours each week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It's a starting point for understanding your base earnings.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Weekly pay is your hourly rate × hours per week. So for a 38-hour week:

**Fortnightly gross = (hourly rate × 38) × 2**

This can help you budget between pay cycles.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

Australia has a National Minimum Wage (NMW) that applies to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. From 1 July 2026, the NMW is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates based on classification, industry, and experience.

For example, the Professional Employees Award 2020 covers many graduate and experienced professionals, including those with an MBA degree. Under this award, a **Level 1 Graduate professional** with a 4- or 5-year degree (such as an MBA) has a minimum hourly rate of $34.57, equating to an annual salary of $68,538. More experienced professionals at Level 2 earn $39.77/hour ($78,836 annually), and at Level 3, $43.46/hour ($86,157 annually).

If you hold an **MBA degree salary** expectations often align with these award levels, but your actual pay may be higher depending on your role, industry, and negotiation. Always check the applicable award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) or the Pay and Conditions Tool.

## Casual Loading: 25% on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for missing entitlements like paid leave. When using our [timesheet](/), you enter your **base hourly rate** (the rate before casual loading). If you tick the casual loading checkbox, the tool adds 25% to that rate automatically.

**Important:** Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The tool handles the addition.

For example, if your base rate under the award is $34.57/hour, your casual rate becomes $34.57 × 1.25 = $43.21/hour. The annual equivalent for a full-time casual (38 hours × 52 weeks) would be $43.21 × 38 × 52 = $85,398.96 gross. However, casuals often work fewer or irregular hours, so actual annual earnings may vary.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional contribution your employer makes to your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This is **not deducted from your pay**; it's paid on top.

So if your annual gross salary is $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 into your super account. This is part of your total remuneration package but is not available as take-home pay.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed estimate.

## Example: MBA Graduate Under Professional Employees Award

Let's apply this to an MBA graduate classified at Level 1 (4-year degree) under the Professional Employees Award. The minimum hourly rate is $34.57.

- **Annual gross:** $34.57 × 38 × 52 = $68,538
- **Fortnightly gross:** ($34.57 × 38) × 2 = $2,627.32
- **Super (12%):** $68,538 × 0.12 = $8,224.56 (paid on top)
- **Estimated tax (2026–27):** Approximately $10,000 (including Medicare levy) – see our [tax calculator](/topics/take-home) for precise figures.
- **Estimated take-home:** Around $58,500 per year, or $2,250 per fortnight.

This is a minimum. Many MBA graduates earn above award rates, especially in senior roles. For more accurate figures, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or consult your employer.

## Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculations on this site assume the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For personalised calculations, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool or check the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide.
